title_candidates: OpenAI's new usage map shows ChatGPT shifting from answers to action
summary: OpenAI Signals adds country-level data showing that work chats lean toward producing outputs, while multimedia use and adoption among people over 35 are rising.

primary_source.title: From asking to doing: How the world is putting ChatGPT to work
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: At work, people are more than twice as likely to use ChatGPT to produce an output or complete a task than they are outside work.
Multimedia use accounts for 7.8 percent of messages and is the fastest-growing use category.
The share of messages from people over 35 rose in nearly every measured country and is 5 percent higher than one year earlier.
The release covers individual Free, Go, Plus, and Pro accounts rather than managed organization accounts.

supporting_sources.title: Download data and methodology
key_facts: OpenAI publishes downloadable data under CC BY 4.0.

supporting_sources.title: OpenAI Signals data dictionary
key_facts: The dataset samples 300,000 consumer messages per month, excludes enterprise and Codex messages, uses automated classifiers, and publishes differentially private aggregates.

prerequisites: Five recent non-sensitive AI prompts, or five sample tasks

steps.instruction: Classify five prompts as asking for information or producing an output, then rewrite one asking prompt as a concrete, verifiable deliverable.
Keep the pattern only if independent source checks show it saves a real step without hiding uncertainty.

references.title: From asking to doing: How the world is putting ChatGPT to work
references.author: OpenAI

risk_flags: The study is OpenAI's analysis of its own consumer product and does not represent all AI use.
The age result uses self-reported age, and the behavioral categories come from automated classifiers rather than user labels.
Enterprise conversations and Codex are excluded; the article states those limits.
